sections.body: Magnesium supports normal enzyme activity, nerve and muscle function, bone structure and energy metabolism. A normal physiological role is not proof of added benefit from a particular supplement.
sections.form_and_absorption: NIH summarizes small studies with greater absorption than oxide or sulfate. This does not establish a universal best form.
sections.research_and_use: Some medicinal citrate preparations are saline laxatives used for short-term occasional constipation. Do not transfer a laxative regimen to every citrate supplement.
sections.high: Supplemental or medicinal magnesium can cause diarrhea, nausea and abdominal cramping; very large exposures can cause serious toxicity. Impaired kidney function increases risk because magnesium removal is reduced. No personal risk or medication assessment is made.
sections.reference: The US adult upper limit at age 19 and older is 350 mg/day elemental magnesium from supplements and medications, excluding magnesium naturally present in foods and beverages. It is not a target or a total-diet ceiling. Children have age-specific references; medically supervised treatment is separate. No product dose is converted or compared.
sections.limits: Solubility and absorption measurements do not establish superior clinical outcomes. Whole-compound mass is not elemental magnesium. Route, formulation, amount, duration and population matter. Exact aliases below are draft label terms, not a verified product-formulation identity.

sections.body: Magnesium supports normal enzyme activity, nerve and muscle function, bone structure and energy metabolism. A normal physiological role is not proof of added benefit from a particular supplement.
sections.form_and_absorption: Human cognitive test results do not establish that a commercial product delivers more magnesium to the human brain than all other forms.
sections.research_and_use: A six-week 2026 trial randomized 100 adults aged 18–45 with dissatisfied sleep to a specific branded L-threonate preparation or placebo. Some cognitive outcomes improved, while Raven’s testing and wearable-measured sleep outcomes did not differ. An estimated cognitive-age score is not proof of reversed biological aging or dementia prevention. The study used one-tailed outcome significance tests and numerous outcomes; interpretation and independent replication matter.
